basic_identification.full_title: Specification for Cam Levers (कैम लीवर की विशिष्टि)
basic_identification.sector_category: Production and General Engineering / Machine Tools, Machine Tool Elements, and Holding Devices (approved by the Production and General Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Machine Tools, Machine Tool Elements, and Holding Devices Sectional Committee, PGD 35, under the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard specifies the physical dimensions, mechanical tolerances, materials, surface finish, and hardness thresholds for cam levers (eccentric clamping levers) used in combination with cam-operated clamps conforming to IS 6090 : 1984.

version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: None (Developed as a new dedicated specification for standard cam levers)

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, dimensional parameters, and hardness readings must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Specifies dimensions and other requirements for cam levers to be used with cam operated clamps conforming to IS : 6090 - 1984.
The lever body must be manufactured from high-grade case-hardened steel featuring a core tensile strength of 600 to 750 N/mm² to prevent shear fractures under rapid manual load cycles.

The eccentric cam contact face is subjected to intense sliding friction; therefore, the cam portion must be hardened to a minimum surface hardness of 680 HV (Vickers Hardness) to prevent flat-spots or surface pitting.

Standardizes physical proportions: Eccentricity e = 1.50 mm (clamping range finished to N6); Handle Length l = 63 mm; Pin Hole Diameter d = 6 mm (F7 fit); Width h = 16 mm; Cam Major Radius r = 16 mm; Radius r1 = 7.5 mm; Radius r2 = 8 mm; Head Height h1 = 31 mm (approx); and Thickness t = 6 mm.
The lever handle must be entirely free from sharp corners, burrs, forge scale, cracks, or parting-line offsets to protect the machine operator from hand cuts.

Levers must be designated by the name, eccentricity (e), handle length (l), standard number, and material. Example: 'CAM LEVER 3 x 125 IS : 10882 Steel' represents a lever of eccentricity e = 3 mm and handle length l = 125 mm.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10882 : 1984 (Reaffirmed 2022) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing quality requirements, material compositions, hardness limits, and nominal dimensions for cam levers used alongside cam-operated clamps (conforming to IS 6090). Maintained under the Machine Tools, Machine Tool Elements, and Holding Devices Sectional Committee (PGD 35), the standard unifies manual rapid-clamping tooling accessories across national machine shops and toolrooms. It specifies strict dimensional parameters—such as eccentricity (1.50 mm for the standard size), handle length (63 mm), and pin-hole dimensions (6 mm diameter under a precise F7 fit)—and mandates case-hardened steel (600 to 750 N/mm² tensile strength) with a minimum cam-surface hardness of 680 HV to prevent localized deformation. By enforcing smooth, burr-free ergonomic handle finishes and standard designation codes, the standard ensures maximum operator safety and tool durability.
